body:
Cheyne Capital closes its CRECH IX real estate debt fund at £3bn, backed by 73 European loans. Read the details and market outlook.

Global alternative investment manager Cheyne Capital has announced the final close of the ninth vintage of its real estate lending programme, Cheyne Real Estate Credit Holdings (CRECH) IX – capital solutions strategy and adjacent vehicles, with a total fundraise of £3bn.

Having launched with seed investment from a Middle Eastern sovereign wealth fund in 2024, the mature fund has 73 underlying loans of which 16 have already been realised.

The vast majority are senior loans referencing a combination of core, core plus, value-add and development assets spanning multiple asset classes, including office, residential and mixed-use, located in the UK, Spain, France, Italy, Portugal, Ireland, Sweden and Belgium.

Ravi Stickney, managing partner and CIO of real estate at Cheyne Capital, said: “The demand for scalable and reliable real estate financing solutions in Europe has never been more acute. The urgent need for our capital is evidenced by the speed with which CRECH IX and its adjacent vehicles are being deployed. European real estate debt markets have long suffered from a supply/demand imbalance and we are witnessing a further retreat of capital provision in today’s longer-term inflationary and volatile environment.

“We have immense gratitude for the trust and commitment of both our longstanding and new investors; their support enables us to provide borrowers with the capital to create, reposition and retain much-needed productive assets, rehabilitate and repurpose unproductive assets, and recapitalise unsustainable capital structures.”

Stuart Fiertz, co-founder and president of Cheyne Capital, added: “On behalf of Jonathan Lourie and myself, I would also like to thank our investors for their continued support and confidence in Cheyne. The successful close of CRECH IX enables us to maintain our focus on larger transactions where we see less competition from other lenders, leading to more attractive returns than we see in the more crowded, mid-market space. It also allows us to continue partnering with the world’s most established and experienced borrowers who are able to support our loans with significant equity investments in their best-in-class assets.”
